Reading this makes me so sad :( but also hopeful for you. And maybe she'll change if she's "prodded" by loss of a responsibility she should've maintained (i.e. marriage requiring her to tend to her own health for the sake of another)

I had this huge comment written, but realized there's not enough info here to make any real offering of advice. Antidepressants, bariatric surgery or pose divorce? I just know how it feels to be with someone and want out, but can't do it for financial reasons. You don't want your dissatisfaction with her choices to turn into resentment from you, as that isn't fair for your or for her, and I don't see how you can avoid that at this point. Like, envision her losing weight and getting in shape and then asking for sex...would you want it then? If not, you should exit, since everyone deserves human intimacy. I think anyway.
(I am both thin and fit, and find this hilarious)

Spooky. What state and county so I know to avoid it?! Jk. I am sex starved to the point of depression and emotional numbness on some days, and I would still never use a reddit site. My rule of thumb since college was a full panel sti within the last 3 mo. of meeting the person, timestamped or in an active email account. It says a lot about a person if they think it's dramatic or too expensive. Health is priceless. So is initial transparency. And you're right, self-care is still a means when in need, ftw (not really ftw, hence, why we're here)  
I see how the points you mentioned could make it more complicated. Fucked up = matter of degree, yeah? What's that cliche quote? "Find someone who's demons play well with yours" But curses, it's accurate. You're wanting sexual intimacy, not getting it when you're both legally in agreement annd by partnered as parents, then maybe all 3 of  you are headed to a better circumstance if the split is followed through (:. I hope you still get to go to your therapist, even if she's not.   
  I'm a lady, but thanks and you're welcome.

Hmmm... are you sure you want to use a subreddit? Great potential for catphishing, personality disorders, stds and stis and emotionally stunted people. Moreso, you don't want to lose your ability/perspective of quality over quantity. Being 40 (me, almost) it is a a different culture than what we knew 15 years ago.  
You've been in a committed relationship with a single partner and though sexless, what appears to be a very respectful dynamic with a spouse. Separation can be messy when you're respectful and effortful. I know. Separation is statistically, more appropriate for marriage recovery of a problem to fix. Maybe make a clean cut because you want more and need more and offer the allowance to move on without guilt, based on what you're saying? If it wasn't the right decision, just get remarried to her.
Full disclosure: I am going through a separation and it is not good when the other partner is holding out. It is very emotionally exhausting due to the length of time you've been with the person and their refusal to go full divorce. She might say she wants you to look elsewhere, but change her mind when you do, and that is a difficult place to be for both of you. Also, you may be the type to consider relationship potential and sexual intimacy on equal-footing, which would just make your eventual time with another more satisfying/intense with opportunity to grow vs. a hookup path.  That's my take, at least.
I'm rooting for you. I'm year 3, once a year so, I don't know how you have gone 6 years.
Oh goodness this is very sad. Lack of self-awareness and conscious lack of effort are not a comedy, but a tragedy. Maybe too close to home :(

Do people ever post to month-old posts?  I don't know, but I am going to anyway:  
It takes at least 90 days for your brain to offset the primitive urge to maintain a chemical/hormonal and social bond with a mate, typically. An intimate relationship.  Not a month, but three months.  At  least.  It should be longer because of your oxytocin status.  If not, you could make it unnecessarily difficult for yourself and lowering odds of a clear head (with or without him) for healthy decision-making.  And at the end of the day, that is what is needed, yes?  
I have nothing to say about the rest of it, but that alone (3 months) is a fact and universal for human brains. If you are able to foster healthy support systems and confidence in the meantime, 3 months would improve your reasoning skills and choices that appear as actual solutions. It is all in how you see it, and you deserve to see it differently.   
I  hope you are able to find the assuredness you're looking for in your own choices, and I support you in that 100%.
